title: Subjunctive Triggers
summary: Recognize expressions that commonly require the subjunctive, including emotion, doubt, necessity, and indefiniteness.

sections.heading: Desire, emotion, and influence
sections.body: Verbs and expressions of wanting, hoping, preferring, fearing, and requesting often trigger the subjunctive in a **que** clause when the subjects differ.

examples.en: I want you to come early.

examples.pt: Tenho medo que eles se atrasem.
examples.en: I am afraid they will be late.

sections.heading: Doubt, denial, and uncertainty
sections.body: Use the subjunctive after expressions that deny certainty: **duvido que**, **não acho que**, **não tenho certeza de que**, and often **talvez**.

examples.pt: Duvido que ele saiba a resposta.
examples.en: I doubt he knows the answer.
I do not think it is expensive.

examples.pt: Talvez a gente precise de ajuda.

sections.heading: Necessity and impersonal expressions
sections.body: Impersonal expressions such as **é importante que**, **é necessário que**, **é melhor que**, and **basta que** usually take the subjunctive.

examples.en: It is important that everyone participate.

examples.pt: É melhor que você espere aqui.
examples.en: It is better that you wait here.

examples.pt: Basta que ela assine o documento.
examples.en: It is enough that she sign the document.

sections.heading: Indefinite or nonexistent antecedents
sections.body: The subjunctive can appear after relative clauses when the thing or person is unknown, desired, or may not exist.

examples.en: I am looking for someone who speaks Japanese.

examples.pt: Quero um apartamento que tenha varanda.
examples.en: I want an apartment that has a balcony.

examples.pt: Não conheço ninguém que more aqui.
examples.en: I do not know anyone who lives here.

keyPoints: The subjunctive often appears in a dependent que clause.
Desire, emotion, doubt, denial, necessity, and indefiniteness are major triggers.
If the subject is the same, Portuguese often uses an infinitive instead of que + subjunctive.
Não acho que usually takes the subjunctive; acho que usually takes the indicative.
Relative clauses can use the subjunctive when the antecedent is indefinite or nonexistent.

commonMistakes.wrong: É importante que eles chegam cedo.
commonMistakes.right: É importante que eles cheguem cedo.
